authoring.value:
Note that the position vectors of the points $A$, $B$, $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨2,-1,2⟩,\,b=⟨3,-5,1⟩,\,c=⟨1,-4,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨3,-5,1⟩-⟨2,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-4,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨1,-4,-1⟩-⟨2,-1,2⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,-3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot (-1)+(-4)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot (-3)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-3)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{14}{\sqrt{18}\cdot \sqrt{19}} \\  & =\frac{14}{3\sqrt{38}}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{14}{3\sqrt{38}})≈{41}^{∘}.
$$

$$

The $△PQR$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠QPR=\theta .$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13978202/assets/3003f0cb329a8f8ef9bc315c70df4773ac1f0c54843dea1208c68bd0f6227bd1.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ} & =q-p \\  & =⟨1,5,4⟩-⟨0,4,5⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{PR} & =r-p \\  & =⟨2,3,6⟩-⟨0,4,5⟩ \\  & =⟨2,-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{PQ}$ and $\overset{\to }{PR}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{PQ}\cdot \overset{\to }{PR}}{|\overset{\to }{PQ}||\overset{\to }{PR}|} \\  & =\frac{1\cdot 2+1\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot 1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(0)={90}^{∘}.
$$

Note that the position vectors of the points $D$, $E$, $F$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}d=⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩,\,e=⟨{t}^{2},\,2,\,t⟩,\,f=⟨t+3,\,{t}^{2},\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△DEF$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠EDF=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13964292/assets/c9cfb3e84e6f76d243125f2a09246b2a1300a0134e71359bb2b528082f064f93.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{DE}$ and $\overset{\to }{DF}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =e-d \\  & =⟨{t}^{2},\,2,\,t⟩-⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨{t}^{2}-t,\,-3,\,t-3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =f-d \\  & =⟨t+3,\,{t}^{2},\,1⟩-⟨t,\,5,\,3⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,{t}^{2}-5,\,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}=6$, we can solve for $t$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF} & =6 \\ ({t}^{2}-t)\cdot 3+(-3)\cdot ({t}^{2}-5)+(t-3)\cdot (-2) & =6 \\ 3{t}^{2}-3t-3{t}^{2}+15-2t+6 & =6 \\ -5t+21 & =6 \\ -5t & =-15 \\ t & =3\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{DE} & =⟨{3}^{2}-3,-3,3-3⟩ \\  & =⟨6,-3,0⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{DF} & =⟨3,{3}^{2}-5,-2⟩ \\  & =⟨3,4,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{DE}$ and $\overset{\to }{DF}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{DE}\cdot \overset{\to }{DF}}{|\overset{\to }{DE}||\overset{\to }{DF}|} \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{4}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{6}{3\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{29}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{145}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{\sqrt{145}})≈{80.44}^{∘}.
$$

Note that the position vectors of the points $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are

$$
\begin{aligned}a=⟨3t,\,t,\,4⟩,\,b=⟨3t,\,4t,\,3⟩,\,c=⟨5t,\,t+1,\,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The triangle $△ABC$ is shown (schematically) in the diagram below, where we denote $∠BAC=\theta .$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13964292/assets/285b8343208079181ac6036cf9ca16abc974d59b9262878ed40c0da9af5683d0.png)

First, we find the components of $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =⟨3t,\,4t,\,3⟩-⟨3t,\,t,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,3t,\,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =⟨5t,\,t+1,\,5⟩-⟨3t,\,t,\,4⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}=2$, we can solve for $t,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC} & =2 \\ 0\cdot 2t+3t\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 1 & =2 \\ 3t-1 & =2 \\ 3t & =3 \\ t & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨0,3,-1⟩, \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, the cosine of the angle between $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2}{\sqrt{10}\cdot \sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{2}{2\sqrt{15}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{15}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{15}})≈{75}^{∘}.
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot \overset{\to }{AC}}{|\overset{\to }{AB}||\overset{\to }{AC}|} \\  & =\frac{-3\cdot 3+1\cdot 2+1\cdot 6}{\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{3}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-1}{\sqrt{11}\sqrt{49}} \\  & =-\frac{1}{7\sqrt{11}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta = \arccos \left( -\dfrac{1}{7\sqrt{11}} \right) \approx 92.5^\circ.
$$

\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{a\cdot b}{|\,a\,||\,b\,|} \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}}{\sqrt{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}}\sqrt{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{-4}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{6}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{37}} \\  & =-\frac{4}{\sqrt{185}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\theta = \arccos \left( -\dfrac{4}{\sqrt{185}} \right) \approx 107.1^\circ.
$$
